arxiv-1905-12072.title: Second law of thermodynamics for batteries with vacuum state
arxiv-1905-12072.creator: Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Paweł Mazurek, Michał Horodecki
arxiv-1905-12072.description: Abstract In stochastic thermodynamics work is a random variable whose average is bounded by the change in the free energy of the system. In most treatments, however, the work reservoir that absorbs this change is either tacitly assumed or modelled using unphysical systems with unbounded Hamiltonians (i.e. the ideal weight).

arxiv-1908-03057.title: Sim-to-Real Learning for Casualty Detection from Ground Projected Point Cloud Data
arxiv-1908-03057.creator: Roni Permana Saputra, Nemanja Rakicevic, Petar Kormushev
arxiv-1908-03057.description: Abstract This paper addresses the problem of human body detection—particularly a human body lying on the ground (a.k.a. casualty)—using point cloud data. This ability to detect a casualty is one of the most important features of mobile rescue robots, in order for them to be able to operate autonomously.

arxiv-2106-04334.title: Electron Holes in a κ \kappa Distribution Background with Singularities
arxiv-2106-04334.creator: Fernando Haas
arxiv-2106-04334.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Fernando Haas. The pseudo-potential method is applied to derive diverse propagating electron hole structures, in a nonthermal or κ \kappa particle distribution function background. The associated distribution function Ansatz reproduces the Schamel distribution of Schamel2015 in the Maxwellian ( κ → ∞ \kappa\rightarrow\infty ) limit, providing a significant generalization of it for plasmas where superthermal electrons are ubiquitous, such as space plasmas. The pseudo-potential and the nonlinear dispersion relation are evaluated.

arxiv-2108-04729.title: Spectral Robustness for Correlation Clustering Reconstruction in Semi-Adversarial Models
arxiv-2108-04729.creator: Flavio Chierichetti, Alessandro Panconesi, Giuseppe Re, Luca Trevisan
arxiv-2108-04729.description: Abstract Correlation Clustering is an important clustering problem with many applications. We study the reconstruction version of this problem in which one is seeking to reconstruct a latent clustering that has been corrupted by random noise and adversarial modifications. Concerning the latter, there is a standard “post-adversarial” model in the literature, in which adversarial modifications come after the noise.

arxiv-2201-13129.title: Predictions of α \alpha -decay half-lives for neutron-deficient nuclei with the aid of artificial neural network
arxiv-2201-13129.creator: A. A. Saeed, W. A. Yahya, O. K. Azeez
arxiv-2201-13129.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by A. A. Saeed, W. A. Yahya, O. K. Azeez. In recent years, artificial neural network (ANN) has been successfully applied in nuclear physics and some other areas of physics. This study begins with the calculations of α \alpha -decay half-lives for some neutron-deficient nuclei using Coulomb and proximity potential model (CPPM), temperature dependent Coulomb and proximity potential model (CPPMT), Royer empirical formula, new Ren B (NRB) formula, and a trained artificial neural network model ( T A ​ N ​ N T^{ANN} ).

arxiv-2204-00164.title: Filter-based Discriminative Autoencoders for Children Speech Recognition
arxiv-2204-00164.creator: Chiang-Lin Tai, Hung-Shin Lee, Yu Tsao, Hsin-Min Wang
arxiv-2204-00164.description: Abstract Children speech recognition is indispensable but challenging due to the diversity of children’s speech. In this paper, we propose a filter-based discriminative autoencoder for acoustic modeling. To filter out the influence of various speaker types and pitches, auxiliary information of the speaker and pitch features is input into the encoder together with the acoustic features to generate phonetic embeddings.

arxiv-2204-07042.title: Mixed discrete variable Gaussian states
arxiv-2204-07042.creator: Nicolae Cotfas
arxiv-2204-07042.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nicolae Cotfas. The quantum systems with finite-dimensional Hilbert space have several applications and are intensively explored theoretically and experimentally. The mathematical description of these systems follows the analogy with the usual infinite-dimensional case. There exist finite versions for most of the elements used in the continuous case, but (to our knowledge) there does not exist a finite version corresponding to the mixed Gaussian states. Our aim is to fill this gap.

arxiv-2304-09041.title: Joint measurement of the galaxy cluster pressure profile with Planck and SPT-SZ
arxiv-2304-09041.creator: J.-B. Melin, G. W. Pratt
arxiv-2304-09041.description: Abstract We measured the average Compton profile of 461 clusters detected jointly by the South Pole Telescope (SPT) and Planck . The number of clusters included in this analysis is about one order of magnitude larger than in previous analyses.

arxiv-2310-04012.title: Self-injective algebras under derived equivalences
arxiv-2310-04012.creator: Changchang Xi, Jin Zhang ∗
arxiv-2310-04012.description: Abstract . The Nakayama permutations of two derived equivalent, self-injective Artin algebras are conjugate. A different but elementary approach is given to showing that the weak symmetry and self-injectivity of finite-dimensional algebras over an arbitrary field are preserved under derived equivalences. † † ∗ Corresponding author. † † 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 18G80, 16E35, 16D50, Secondary 16G10, 18F30, 16P10.

arxiv-2410-04895.creator: Nicolas Kainz, Dirk Lebiedz
arxiv-2410-04895.description: Abstract . In this follow-up paper to [ 10 ] we investigate the global topology and geometry of dynamical systems x ˙ = F ⁡ ( x ) \dot{x}=F(x) with entire vector field F F by exploiting and extending the local structure of finite elliptic decompositions.

arxiv-2410-13428.title: Generate and Instantiate What You Prefer: Text-Guided Diffusion for Sequential Recommendation
arxiv-2410-13428.creator: Guoqing Hu, Zhengyi Yang, Zhibo Cai, An Zhang, Xiang Wang
arxiv-2410-13428.description: Abstract . Recent advancements in generative recommendation systems, particularly in the realm of sequential recommendation tasks, have shown promise in enhancing generalization to new items. Among these approaches, diffusion-based generative recommendation has emerged as an effective tool, leveraging its ability to capture data distributions and generate high-quality samples.

arxiv-2411-10136.title: CoSAM: Self-Correcting SAM for Domain Generalization in 2D Medical Image Segmentation
arxiv-2411-10136.creator: Yihang Fu Ziyang Chen Yiwen Ye Xingliang Lei Zhisong Wang Yong Xia
arxiv-2411-10136.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yihang Fu Ziyang Chen Yiwen Ye Xingliang Lei Zhisong Wang Yong Xia. Medical images often exhibit distribution shifts due to variations in imaging protocols and scanners across different medical centers. Domain Generalization (DG) methods aim to train models on source domains that can generalize to unseen target domains. Recently, the segment anything model (SAM) has demonstrated strong generalization capabilities due to its prompt-based design, and has gained significant attention in image segmentation tasks.

arxiv-2504-21311.title: Covert Prompt Transmission for Secure Large Language Model Services Thanks: R. Zhang, Y. Liu, S. Tang, J. Wang, and D. Niyato are with the College of Computing and Data Science, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (e-mail: ruichen.zhang@ntu.edu.sg, yinqiu001@e.ntu.edu.sg, n2409411h@e.ntu.edu
arxiv-2504-21311.creator: Ruichen Zhang, Yinqiu Liu, Shunpu Tang, Jiacheng Wang, Dusit Niyato
arxiv-2504-21311.description: Abstract This paper investigates covert prompt transmission for secure and efficient large language model (LLM) services over wireless networks. We formulate a latency minimization problem under fidelity and detectability constraints to ensure confidential and covert communication by jointly optimizing the transmit power and prompt compression ratio.

arxiv-2509-00074.title: Language and Experience: A Computational Model of Social Learning in Complex Tasks
arxiv-2509-00074.creator: Cédric Colas, Tracey Mills, Ben Prystawski, Michael Henry Tessler, Noah Goodman, Jacob Andreas, Joshua Tenenbaum
arxiv-2509-00074.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Cédric Colas, Tracey Mills, Ben Prystawski, Michael Henry Tessler, Noah Goodman, Jacob Andreas, Joshua Tenenbaum. The ability to combine linguistic guidance from others with direct experience is central to human development, enabling safe and rapid learning in new environments. How do people integrate these two sources of knowledge, and how might AI systems? We present a computational framework that models social learning as joint probabilistic inference over structured, executable world models given sensorimotor and linguistic data.

arxiv-2509-07408.title: SKR Analysis of MIMO FSO Systems with One- and Two-way CV-QKD Protocols in Hybrid Quantum Noise Environment
arxiv-2509-07408.creator: Sushil Kumar, Soumya P. Dash, George C. Alexandropoulos
arxiv-2509-07408.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sushil Kumar, Soumya P. Dash, George C. Alexandropoulos. A multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) communication system is considered in this paper, which supports the secret key transmission between two legitimate users, Alice and Bob, by employing continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD). The wireless channels are subjected to the effects of atmospheric turbulence that lead to beam spreading, pointing error, and turbulence-induced fading, which, along with the presence of hybrid quantum noise, negatively impact the secret key exchange between Alice and Bob.

arxiv-2510-24962.title: An Extreme Scattering Event Toward PSR J2313+4253 psrchive ( Hotan et al. 2004 ) , pypulse ( Lam 2017 ) , scintools ( Reardon et al. 2020 ) , scipy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 ) , numpy ( van der Walt et al. 2011 ) , matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , ultranest ( Buchner 2021 )
arxiv-2510-24962.creator: Zachary C. Zelensky, Jacob E. Turner, Juan G. Lebron Medina, Daniel E. Reichart, Joshua B. Haislip, Vladimir V. Kouprianov, Steve White, Frank Ghigo, Sue Ann Heatherly, Maura A. McLaughlin
arxiv-2510-24962.description: Abstract We present evidence of an extreme scattering event (ESE) toward PSR J2313+4253 using high-cadence observations taken with the Green Bank Observatory 20m telescope. The high density of observations in time allow for detailed tracking of the event. We observe a pair of caustic spikes along with the characteristic drop in scintillation bandwidth that is expected during an ESE.

arxiv-2601-16311.title: A Non-Autonomous Model for Parabolic Implosion
arxiv-2601-16311.creator: Katelynn Huneycutt, Samantha Sandberg-Clark, Liz Vivas
arxiv-2601-16311.description: Abstract . Orthogonal polynomials appear naturally in the study of compositions of Möbius transformations. In this paper, we consider several classes of orthogonal polynomials associated to non-autonomous perturbations of a parabolic Möbius map. Our results can be viewed as instances of non-autonomous parabolic implosion, including a random perturbative regime in which convergence holds almost surely. 1.

arxiv-2602-06674.description: Abstract . High-quality annotated datasets are crucial for advancing machine learning in medical image analysis. However, a critical gap exists: most datasets either offer a single, clean ground truth, which hides real-world expert disagreement, or they provide multiple annotations without a separate gold standard for objective evaluation.

pmc-11710493.title: Impact of Abnormal Phosphorylation on the Oligomerization of Tau Repeat R2
pmc-11710493.creator: Viet H Man
pmc-11710493.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundReversible post‐translational modifications, phosphorylation and dephosphorylation, on tau protein play a critical role in the microtubule (MT) modulation. However, abnormal tau phosphorylation, which occurs in tauopathies such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD), causes the dissociation of tau from MTs. The dissociated tau then aggregates into sequent forms from soluble oligomers to paired helical filaments (PHF), and insoluble neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs), a hallmark of AD.

pmc-11772163.title: Discussion on the optimization of personalized medication using information systems based on pharmacogenomics: an example using colorectal cancer
pmc-11772163.creator: Mengying Yuan, Yuankun Zheng, Fei Wang, Niuniu Bai, Haoling Zhang, Yuan Bian, Hao Liu, Xia He
pmc-11772163.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Pharmacogenomics (PGx) is a powerful tool for clinical optimization of drug efficacy and safety. However, due to many factors affecting drugs in the real world, PGx still accounts for a small proportion of actual clinical application scenarios. Therefore, based on the information software, pharmacists use their professional advantages to integrate PGx into all aspects of pharmaceutical care, which is conducive to promoting the development of personalized medicine.

pmc-12449062.title: Physiological and molecular responses to high-temperature stress at anthesis in Brazilian flooded rice
pmc-12449062.creator: Silmara da Luz Correia, Kanjana Laosuntisuk, Jigar Desai, Paulo Regis Ferreira da Silva, Carla Andrea Delatorre, Colleen J Doherty, Kate McCulloh, Showkat Ganie
pmc-12449062.description: High-temperature events are projected to increase in frequency under future climate scenarios, threatening rice yields globally. This study investigated the physiological and molecular responses of two Brazilian flooded rice varieties, IRGA 428 and BR-IRGA 409, during the anthesis stage under high-temperature stress, aiming to uncover mechanisms of heat tolerance.

pmc-13202684.title: Responsible digital transformation in rural primary healthcare services: critical factors from a Norwegian case study
pmc-13202684.creator: Raj Kumar Thapa, Trond Bliksvær, Trude Fløystad Eines, Merete Kvamme Fabritius, Cecilie Katrine Utheim Grønvik, Solrun Holm, Nadra Jesmine Nilsen, Finn Robert Verlo, Trude Hartviksen
pmc-13202684.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo explore the critical factors that shape the potential for co-creating and implementing a virtual department for home-based healthcare in a rural municipality.MethodsA qualitative case study was conducted in a rural municipality in Northern Norway. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, focus groups, and co-creation workshops involving healthcare leaders, frontline staff, service users and relatives, and representative from the pensioners’ federation.

pmc-13384564.title: Physically mixed graphene aerogel:carbon black (GA:CB)-supported Pt or hydrothermally synthesized GA-Pt/CB hybrid electrocatalysts for PEM fuel cells
pmc-13384564.creator: Emine TEKE ÖNER, Melis Irmak AYDIN, Merve Nida DURSUNOĞLU, Ayşe BAYRAKÇEKEN
pmc-13384564.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Graphene aerogels (GAs), having the superior properties of graphene and aerogel structures, are promising support materials for Pt nanoparticles to be used as electrocatalysts for PEM fuel cells. In this study, two routes were followed to synthesize GA-based electrocatalysts. In the first route, after GA synthesis it was physically mixed with carbon black (CB) by changing the mass ratios from 0% to 100% with 25% increments and then decorated with Pt nanoparticles via microwave irradiation, resulting in Pt/GA:CB electrocatalysts.
